errors.evidence: The data points on the x-axis extend to approximately layer 38, not just to 35.

errors.text_span: From Layer 1 to Layer 35, the values continue to decline gradually
errors.evidence: This is an over-generalization of the trend. The decline from Layer 1 to approximately Layer 5 is still quite steep, not gradual. The decline only becomes gradual after about Layer 5.
The value at Layer 35 is very close to 0.00, not 0.05. Given the y-axis scale, 0.05 is a significant overestimation.

errors.text_span: and remain nearly flat for the remainder of the layers
errors.evidence: This is misleading. The curve becomes nearly flat starting around layer 20, not after layer 35 as the phrasing implies.
